title: Modifiers: the order matters, and the ones that only look alike

videos.script: Text, then padding, then a yellow background. Swap the last two, and the yellow shrinks. Same words, different screen. {{wrap}} That is because a modifier does not change a view. It returns a new view, with the old one inside. {{order}} So a chain of modifiers is a set of boxes, one inside the next, and each box sees only what is inside it. {{alike}} Some modifiers look alike and are different boxes. An overlay and a ZStack. Hidden, and an if. {{custom}} Then you give a chain a name, so three screens can share it. {{env}} And you meet the modifiers that reach down the whole tree instead, like a font. {{trap}} Then the trap. A helper that applies a modifier only sometimes, and quietly costs the view its identity. {{model}} And finally you build the wrappers yourself, in plain Swift, and print the size each box reports.
